status: Version 1, 4 November 2026. Sources: every paper.src.html (else paper.html) in papers/, the paper cards of dictospheres.com, the DICTOnary atom cards and the cross-links audit of 4 November; papers to #94. Each new paper, read or test is one edit to concordance.json and a rebuild; new versions are batched.

Not yet covered: the books as entries of their own; the findings F1–F21 except where a paper, card or DICTOnary entry names them; the Kaleidohedra app Almanac (alm.c.*), whose concept ids these could feed later; every piece of every kit (only pieces with a name are listed).
To check (threads): the seed list of the four-dimensional queens named #64, which is The Swap Rule in Crystals; it is replaced here by #62 and #63. There is no card numbered #82, #46 or #21.

To check (dates): for #8–#38a the local texts carry only the date of their current version (20 October 2026, the licence change); #1–#20, #27 and #31a–#35b have no text of their own in papers/ (findings, book chapters or short records): their lines come from the site cards.

Names: every name is DICTO's choice unless a paper says otherwise (DICTO, 4 November 2026). Fallen Humpty (D102): the DICTOnary gives #62, the name is also in #63. Golden Clasp (D107) first appears in a study, not a paper.

Name clash: “golden tetrahedra” of #38a (Danzer, Mosseri–Sadoc) are not the Golden Cut Tetrahedra of #88/#89. The TI Star core (D105) is cut at (10 − √5)/19 of each edge (#78 version 3); the DICTOnary draft is corrected, the published Golden Cycle and Star Cores books at their next versions.
To check (the triangle): the placement of each thread on page “The Singularity” is the compiler's reading of the papers, for DICTO to confirm.

Part 5B: every outside find was checked against its abstract or a reliable record (column “checked”); none is yet read in full, all stand “to read”. Unrefereed preprints found by the search are left out. Library copies: only Hermann is held so far.

concepts.name: golden cut
concepts.definition: Cutting every corner of a solid equally so that each face becomes a truncated polygon with its sides in the golden ratio φ (#88).
concepts.by: DICTO's observation of the 3-fold hexagon in his solids; the solids and family names are DICTO's (#88)

concepts.name: truncated triangle
concepts.definition: A hexagon with all six angles 120° and sides alternating between two lengths; the regular hexagon is the case of equal sides (#88).
concepts.by: classical face; DICTO observed that it runs through his solids (#88)

concepts.name: pyramidise (centre pyramids)
concepts.definition: Split a solid whose centre lies inside every face plane into its centre pyramids, one cone from the centre over each face (#44, #87).
concepts.by: Aristotle's pyramid (classical); DICTO proposed pyramidise as one operation on any such solid (#87)

concepts.name: Star and Star Halo
concepts.definition: Turn a solid’s face pyramids outwards and it becomes a star; the tightest skin round the tips is the star’s halo (#79).
concepts.by: DICTO's idea (#78); the name Star Halo is DICTO's

concepts.name: valley rule
concepts.definition: Shorten each spike just enough to clear its neighbours: the ridges keep full spikes and the valleys flatten (#79).

concepts.name: core turn (core cycle)
concepts.definition: The solid common to the hulls of the tips of each family of faces; for the truncated icosahedron it alternates, and two turns give it back (#81).
concepts.by: DICTO found it for TI (#78) and proposed it for every two-family solid (#81)

concepts.name: growth rule T
concepts.definition: Every corner v of a solid gives the face plane v·x = v·v, through v and at right angles to the line from the centre; T(S) is the solid these planes bound (#39).
concepts.by: DICTO's growth rule (#80); T is the 3D form of the classical antipedal construction (#38 v3)

concepts.name: reverse step P
concepts.definition: The step back: take as new corners the foot points of the face planes, the points of those planes nearest the centre (#39).
concepts.by: DICTO proposed running the rule the other way (#39)

concepts.name: polar reciprocation
concepts.definition: Replace each solid by its polar reciprocal: the nesting of a cycle reverses (#32).
concepts.by: classical; turning the cycle inside out by it was DICTO's idea (#32)

concepts.name: the sweep S(μ) = P ∩ μP*
concepts.definition: The flats y = x/μ of the product P × P* of a solid and its polar cut out P ∩ μP*; every corner cut of P or P* is such a section (#91).
concepts.by: DICTO proposed cube × octahedron as the six-dimensional home of the pair (#90) and following each solid with its dual through the dimensions (#91)

concepts.name: weight walk (power cell)
concepts.definition: Each piece is the region nearer, in a weighted sense, to its own point than to any other; one number, a weight given to one kind of point against the other, slides (#52, #53).
concepts.by: power diagrams are classical (Aurenhammer); DICTO's two loops read this way (#52)

concepts.name: web of bonds
concepts.definition: Draw one line, a bond, between every two pieces that share a face; the lines make a web, the classical weighted Delaunay web (#52).

concepts.name: DICTONIC SOLIDS and BONDS
concepts.definition: The six convex and keyed solids of #48 and #51, held in three bonds (#51).

concepts.name: Delian bond
concepts.definition: The cut of the octet’s double cones at which the two solids have the same volume: the tetrahedron’s has doubled and the octahedron’s halved (#51).
concepts.by: DICTO proposed the approach and named Samson and Delilah; doubling is the ancient Delian problem (#51)

concepts.name: golden split
concepts.definition: Cut each AXE into four little pyramids from one inner point and give each to the piece it touches; at 1/φ along its axis nothing sticks out (#48).
concepts.by: DICTO: pieces without odd protrusions, cuts "hemispherical, or anywhere in between" (#48)

concepts.name: shadow forms
concepts.definition: Other ways of breaking up the same space, to find new pieces (#48).

concepts.name: keys and dents
concepts.definition: A key or a dent moves small pieces from one solid to its partner; keys change the pieces but never the network (#54, #56).
concepts.by: DICTO (keyed glue, #37; keyed versions of the new pairs, #56)

concepts.name: c/h stacking words
concepts.definition: Each layer sits on the one below as in the octet (c) or as its mirror image (h); any word in c and h is a stacking (#40).
concepts.by: Jagodzinski's notation (classical); taking the OG family to every stacking was proposed by Claude and adopted by DICTO (#40)

concepts.name: Fibonacci stacking
concepts.definition: Layers c and h in the never-repeating order of c → ch, h → c; the hexagonal share is exactly 1/φ² (#69).

concepts.name: Rule of Halves
concepts.definition: A tetrahedral gap takes the piece of the pure stacking of its nearest layer; an octahedral gap's piece is two halves, from the layers above and below (#57).
concepts.by: DICTO (#84 credit); DICTO's idea to follow the web onto every stacking (#57)

concepts.name: Janus c/h pieces
concepts.definition: Octahedral pieces with one cubic and one hexagonal half, looking into one stacking above and the other below (#57).

concepts.name: Swap Rule
concepts.definition: The two mixed pieces always add up to the two pure ones (#61).

concepts.name: Hexagonality Law
concepts.definition: In every stacking each kind of piece totals exactly what its layers hold in their own pure stackings, a straight line in the share of hexagonal layers (#66).

concepts.name: Window Law
concepts.definition: Anything fixed by g consecutive layers has a mean that is linear in the shares of the c/h words of length g (#84).

concepts.name: Splash Rules
concepts.definition: Look for one simple rule behind a whole family of exactly computed values (#84).

concepts.name: HexOct layer tiles
concepts.definition: The tile of a layer is its share of space, four pieces; only two tiles, c and h, occur in any stacking (#75).

concepts.name: tower move
concepts.definition: Moving one tower of the c-tile by one lattice step along its own layer joins the towers along a face (#86).

concepts.name: knitting slice
concepts.definition: One plane, perpendicular to a row of touching balls, cuts every tetrahedron into an isosceles triangle and every octahedron into a rhombus, a chart to knit (#83).

concepts.name: face-to-face reduction
concepts.definition: In every face-to-face tiling by face pyramids, the pyramids round each apex make up their whole solid (#77).

concepts.name: Vacuus: SHEETS and STRUTS
concepts.definition: Keep only the walls between the centre pyramids, a fin O–A–B for each edge; built as SHEETS (the fins) and STRUTS (a rod from the centre to every corner, with the edges) (#87).

concepts.name: field obstruction
concepts.definition: The Golden Cut Cubes need Q(√2, √5), so no point set with coordinates in Q(√5) holds a similar copy of one (#90).

concepts.name: cut equals shadow
concepts.definition: Asking the cut to equal the shadow of a lattice orbit selects μ = φ, where the roots of D6 cast the Icosaxes point for point (#90).

concepts.name: tight cycles
concepts.definition: Nestings in which every step is tight; one that closes at a power of φ is a DICTO Golden Tight Cycle (#34, #91).
concepts.by: see #34; the name DICTO Golden Tight Cycles is DICTO’s (#91)

concepts.name: golden cycle
concepts.definition: An exact, endlessly repeating nesting of icosahedral solids, each layer filled by a few repeated pieces, growing by φ³ each turn (#22, #23).

concepts.name: gnomon
concepts.definition: The piece which, added to a figure, makes a whole of the same shape, only larger (Euclid, Heron) (#54).
concepts.by: classical; DICTO's idea to carry it into his three-dimensional golden cycle (#54)

concepts.name: EKP construction
concepts.definition: Put Euclid's six roofs on a cube and reflect the roof corners back through the cube faces: they land on a regular icosahedron inside (#8).

concepts.name: Kagome hull test
concepts.definition: Group cells into hull-shaped clusters and ask whether any two share at most one piece and every shared piece lies in exactly two (#17).

concepts.name: Dehn invariant (counting)
concepts.definition: A polyhedron that tiles space has Dehn invariant zero; #44 makes a Dehn-type count on dihedral angles rigorous with the Splitting Theorem of Conway, Radin and Sadun.

concepts.name: spinel twin law
concepts.definition: Twinning on an octahedron-face plane by a half-turn about ⟨111⟩; for OG the twin is OG turned 60° (#37a).

concepts.name: polyhedral stretching
concepts.definition: Slide a solid in a straight line and take the shape it sweeps through (#49).

concepts.name: lattice moves
concepts.definition: A shear of the lattice, the equal-edged cell and a stretch rebuild classical space-fillers in one setting (#50).
concepts.by: Fedorov's moves (1885); DICTO's idea that they rebuild the cut-and-glue fillers (#50)

concepts.name: Reuleaux construction
concepts.definition: A ball on every corner of a Platonic solid, radius the solid's diameter; the body is what all the balls share (#45).
